papers.title_in_file: Surrogate optimization of variational quantum circuits
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, results, outlook; appendices skimmed only
papers.what_it_is: A surrogate-Hessian line search that optimizes VQE circuit parameters using a classical approximate simulator, tested on molecules, spin models and a 40-qubit IBM run.

assertions.value: The authors report that their surrogate line-search optimizer outperforms the Powell optimizer by a factor of 2 to 4 in the cases they studied in the presence of sampling noise.
quotes: this new optimizer outperforms the Powell optimizer by a factor of 2 to 4 in the cases we studied in the presence of sampling noise
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from the authors' own case studies (molecules and spin models).
assertions.reader_inference: The factor applies only to the cases studied; no wider claim is made.

assertions.value: The authors report a proof-of-principle run on ibm brisbane for a transverse Ising model using 40 qubits, in which the parameters converged to 2.5 standard deviations of the expected result and, without noise, give results within 1% of the ansatz minimum, while the measured energies are well above the expected values.
assertions.anchor: Section IV and V. Outlook, pp.6-7; Fig. 4
quotes: a proof of principle demonstration was performed on ibm brisbane for a transverse Ising model using 40 qubits
the parameters have converged to 2.5 standard deviations of the expected result and, in the absence of noise, give results within 1% of the ansatz minimum
Although the energies extracted from the simulation are well above the expected values
assertions.certainty_reason: One hardware run reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardware energies were not accurate; only the converged parameters matched.

assertions.value: The authors state that the efficacy of the line search is contingent upon accurate conjugate search directions from the low-level theory Hessian, and that it struggles when negative eigenvalues appear in the surrogate's Hessian.
quotes: The efficacy of this line search optimization is contingent upon accurate conjugate search directions being obtained from Hessian in the low-level theory
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of the method's limit, Outlook p.7.

papers.title_in_file: Quantizing graphs, one way or two?
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction and conclusion; body skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A mathematical-physics review comparing two ways to quantize a graph (self-adjoint Hamiltonian versus vertex scattering matrices).
papers.why_not: Pure mathematical physics of quantum graphs; it does not mention quantum computing, qubits or machine learning.

papers.title_in_file: Sequence Processing with Quantum Tensor Networks
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, model definitions, results, hardware section, discussion; appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: Tree-structured tensor network models built from parameterised quantum circuits for binary sequence classification, run in simulation and on Quantinuum H2-1.

assertions.value: The authors report test accuracies of 89.0% for the uCTN model and 94.0% for the hCTN model on the DNA binding dataset, with very few trainable parameters.
quotes: For the uCTN achieving 89.0% test, the number of trainable parameters is 3/token and 11 in the remaining architecture
For the hCTN achieving 94.0% test, the number of trainable parameters is 3/token
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on one dataset.

assertions.value: The authors report that on Quantinuum's H2-1 processor, of 50 Clickbait circuits only 1 disagreed with its classical simulation on the classification label, and that the 64-qubit uCTN circuit was compressed to an 11-qubit circuit by qubit reuse.
quotes: From the 50 Clickbait circuits executed on H2-1, we find that only 1 disagrees with its classical simulation regarding the classification label
the 64-qubit uCTN circuit is compressed down to an 11-qubit circuit
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical hardware result from one study; only a selection of test examples was executed.
assertions.reader_inference: Agreement was measured against classical simulation, not a hardware advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tensor network topology of their models allows efficient tensor contraction, making the models classically simulable.
quotes: allows for efficient tensor contraction strategies, thus making them classically simulable
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its models' scope, Section 2, p.3.
assertions.reader_inference: The models as defined give no quantum advantage over classical simulation of training and inference.

assertions.value: The authors claim that this work constitutes the first scalable implementation of near-term quantum language processing.
quotes: This work constitutes the first scalable implementation of near-term quantum language processing
assertions.certainty_reason: Priority claim by the authors, who are partly affiliated with Quantinuum.

papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, Fashion-MNIST experiment section, discussion; theory sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A scheme that replaces trainable circuit parameters with ensembles of fixed circuits and observables combined by classical convex optimization.

assertions.value: The authors report that on a binary coat-versus-shirt Fashion-MNIST task, all post-variational methods exceed the variational algorithm when the same Ansatz is used, training on 200 samples and testing on 50 samples from each class.
quotes: Our results show that all post-variational methods exceed the variational algorithm while using the same Ansatz
training on 200 samples and testing on 50 samples from each class
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small simulated experiment.
assertions.reader_inference: A small binary task; it does not show a general advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that, given a selected set of fixed Ansatze, the post-variational method involves only convex optimization and can guarantee a global minimum solution in polynomial time in the size of that set.
quotes: the post-variational method involves only convex optimization, and hence can provide a guarantee of finding a global minimum solution in polynomial time
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors' argument, conditioned on the chosen Ansatz set.
assertions.reader_inference: The guarantee is conditional; the hard choice of Ansatz set remains.

assertions.value: The authors state that they do not claim to resolve barren plateau problems or related exponential concentration, and that they do not exhibit a proven quantum advantage.
quotes: we do not claim to resolve barren plateau problems or related exponential concentration stemming from the exponentially large Hilbert space
we do not exhibit a quantum advantage that is proven
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of limits, Discussion pp.12-13.

assertions.value: The authors report that post-variational algorithms extract more features than the classical algorithm, leading to more parameters to optimize and overfitting to a certain extent, shown by decreasing testing accuracy.
quotes: there are more parameters to optimize, leading to overfitting on the training model to a certain extent
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical observation from one experiment.

papers.title_in_file: Generalized quantum geometric tensor for excited states using the path integral approach
papers.partial_detail: abstract and introduction; keyword search for quantum computing, qubit, variational and machine learning found no hits
papers.what_it_is: A path-integral formulation of the quantum geometric tensor for ground and excited states, with curvature calculations for several quantum systems.
papers.why_not: Theoretical quantum mechanics of parameter-space geometry; it has no quantum computing or machine learning workload.

papers.title_in_file: Almost fault-tolerant quantum machine learning with drastic overhead reduction
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, numerical results summary, discussion; appendices skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of partial quantum error correction for QML in which only two-qubit Clifford gates are assumed error-corrected and magic state distillation is omitted.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 75-layer variational classifier trained on the 10-class MNIST dataset remained trainable under single-qubit depolarizing noise at a level they describe as comparable to state-of-the-art quantum computers, with performance only slightly degraded compared to the fully fault-tolerant case in simulation.
quotes: To demonstrate the operation of our scheme, we selected the 10-class MNIST dataset
We experimentally demonstrate the trainability of the QVC75 model (a model with 75 variational layers) for a single-qubit gate error rate comparable to that of state-of-the-art quantum computers
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Results are from noisy simulation, not hardware.

assertions.value: The authors state that the result assumes error-corrected two-qubit Controlled-Z gates (Clifford operations).
quotes: By assuming error-corrected two-qubit Controlled-Zs (Clifford operations)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that performance was poor when both single- and two-qubit noise was turned on, and that they do not deny the overall trend predicted by noise-induced barren plateaus as noise becomes stronger.
quotes: the poor performance when both single- and two-qubit noise was turned on further reinforces the necessity of partial quantum error correction
this does not deny the overall trend predicted by the noise-induced barren plateaus as the noise becomes stronger
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of limits, Section IV.

papers.title_in_file: Efficient parameterised compilation for hybrid quantum programming
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, results, conclusion; implementation sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: OpenQLPC, an explicit-parameter extension to OpenQL that avoids recompiling the whole program in each iteration of hybrid algorithms such as VQE.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the MAXCUT benchmark, compilation of hybrid algorithms with OpenQLPC is up to two times faster than with PyQuil or Qiskit, and that in the full benchmark the improvements decrease accumulated compilation time by 40 to 70%.
quotes: When using OpenQLPC, compilation of hybrid algorithms is up to two times faster than when using PyQuil or Qiskit
in OpenQLPC result in a decrease of 40 to 70% in (accumulated) compilation time
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark from one study on one algorithm (MAXCUT).
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract and the conclusion give different speed-up factors for the same comparison, so the figure depends on the measure used.

assertions.value: The authors report that for total execution time of the MAXCUT benchmark the simulator has more influence than compile time, and that the Qiskit Aer simulator is 2 to 3 times as fast as the QX simulator used by OpenQL and OpenQLPC.
quotes: the performance of the simulators used has more influence than the compile times of the languages
the Qiskit Aer simulator is 2 to 3 times as fast as the QX simulator used by OpenQL and OpenQLPC
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The compile-time gain does not make OpenQLPC fastest end to end in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that when simulating quantum algorithms on classical computers the simulation time can be excessively large, which limits the impact of their approach, and that the impact becomes significant on real quantum devices.
quotes: the simulation time can be excessively large as expected, which limits the impact of the improvement achieved by our approach
assertions.certainty_reason: The statement about real devices is a projection; no hardware run is reported.
assertions.reader_inference: The benefit on real hardware is asserted, not measured in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: A Novel Noise-Aware Classical Optimizer for Variational Quantum Algorithms
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, algorithm overview, numerical results, discussion; proofs skimmed
papers.what_it_is: ANATRA, a noise-aware derivative-free model-based trust-region optimizer for variational quantum algorithms, with a convergence analysis and QAOA MaxCut tests.

assertions.value: The authors state that, building on previous results, they proved that with high probability their method exhibits a worst-case convergence rate to a neighborhood of a local minimum, provided the neighborhood size is greater than a function of the noise level.
quotes: Building on previous results, we proved that with high probability our method exhibits a worst-case
assertions.certainty_reason: A proof stated in the paper's theory sections and summarised in Section 6, p.30; the coordinator should confirm the theorem number.
assertions.reader_inference: The proof assumes a zeroth-order oracle with bounded or subexponential noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that on simulated QAOA MaxCut problems there is little distinction, but perhaps a slight preference for PyBOBYQA, at 1000 shots per evaluation, and an increasingly clear preference for ANATRA as the shot count decreases.
quotes: In less noisy settings (when the shot count is 1000 shots per evaluation), there is little distinction, but perhaps a slight preference, for using PyBOBYQA over ANATRA
as the noise increases (the shot count decreases), we see an increasingly clear preference for employing ANATRA
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from simulations on two small MaxCut instances.

assertions.value: The authors report a hardware experiment on IBM Algiers for the toy-graph QAOA MaxCut instance only, with only the two best-performing solvers because of time and budget constraints, and state that the relative advantage of ANATRA over PyBOBYQA clearly increased in this noisier setting.
quotes: Due to time and budget constraints, we only ran this second set of experiments with the two best-performing solvers
the relative advantage of using ANATRA over PyBOBYQA has clearly increased in this noisier setting
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one small hardware experiment.

assertions.value: The authors state that using the standard error of cost function estimates to estimate the noise level in the presence of gate noise is not entirely technically correct, and that more robust estimation is a topic for future research.
quotes: Although not entirely technically correct, it is reasonable to continue using the standard error of cost function estimates to estimate
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of a limit, Section 5, p.30.
